input: Figure out my Myers-Briggs type properly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: MBTI can mean just getting a 4-letter result, or it can include understanding each dichotomy deeply, reading type descriptions, and verifying fit — knowing the scope shapes how thorough the plan needs to be.
Whether the user has taken tests before (and doubts the results) or is starting from scratch completely changes where the plan begins.
Is this purely self-directed, or does the user want external input — e.g., asking people who know them well to validate, or working with a certified MBTI practitioner?
A certified MBTI assessment costs money; free online tests vary wildly in quality. Budget determines which resources are on the table.
Some people want a confident single type; others want to understand where they fall on each spectrum. Defining 'done well' shapes the depth of research needed.
Some people prefer reading and self-reflection; others prefer watching videos, taking multiple tests, or journaling. This determines the format of the activities in the plan.
Knowing how much time the user is willing to invest per session and overall determines whether this is a one-afternoon task or a weeks-long reflective process.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to accurately identify their MBTI personality type, going beyond a surface-level result to feel confident in their type.

questions.title: Have you taken an MBTI test before, and do you doubt the result?
questions.description: Establish the user's starting point — whether this is a first attempt or a re-evaluation of a result they're unsure about.

questions.title: What does 'properly' mean to you — what would satisfy you?
questions.description: Clarify the success criteria: is it a confident 4-letter type, a nuanced understanding of each dimension, or something else?

questions.title: Should this cover all four dichotomies or focus on specific ones?
questions.description: Define the scope — does the user want a full type profile or are they mainly confused about one or two dimensions (e.g., I/E or J/P)?

questions.title: Are you open to paying for an official assessment or sticking to free resources?
questions.description: Determine the budget constraint, which decides whether a certified practitioner or official Myers-Briggs tool is part of the plan.

questions.title: Do you want input from people who know you, or keep this self-directed?
questions.description: Clarify who is involved — purely solo reflection, or incorporating perspectives from friends, family, or a professional.

questions.title: Do you prefer reading, self-reflection exercises, videos, or taking multiple tests?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred learning and discovery style to tailor the format of activities in the plan.

questions.title: How much total time are you willing to spend on this?
questions.description: Establish the time budget — a single focused session versus a gradual multi-week process of reflection and research.
